storyContent: Understanding the Node.js event loop is the foundation of building high-performance backends. The event loop offloads I/O to the system kernel while keeping the main thread free. It runs through phases: timers, pending callbacks, idle, poll, check, and close callbacks. Mastering this unlocks massive throughput gains.
storySummary: Deep dive into Node.js event loop phases and async concurrency
commentContent: This is one of the most thorough breakdowns I have read. The event loop explanation finally cleared things up for our team!

storyContent: Choosing the right index in PostgreSQL can be the difference between a 2ms query and a 2 second one. B-Tree indexes handle equality and range queries. GIN handles JSONB and full-text vectors. BRIN is best for huge append-only tables with naturally ordered timestamps. Always verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
storySummary: Practical guide to B-Tree GIN and BRIN index types

storyContent: Running EXPLAIN ANALYZE on your slowest queries is the fastest way to find missing indexes and poor join strategies. Nested Loop joins work well for small inner sets. Hash Joins are best for larger unindexed datasets. Merge Joins are optimal when both sides are pre-sorted.
storySummary: How to read and optimize PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE output
commentContent: I tested this in staging and it worked perfectly. Pub/Sub messages now deliver in under 5ms across all instances.

storyContent: Domain-Driven Design separates pure business entities from database ORM models. Define repository interfaces inside the domain core so your business logic never imports TypeORM directly. This makes unit test coverage achievable without a real database.

storyContent: Never rename a column in a single deployment. Use the expand-contract pattern. First add the new column and write to both. Then backfill historical rows in small batches. Finally switch reads to new column and drop the old one in the next release.
storySummary: Zero-downtime schema changes using expand and contract migrations
commentContent: Loved the practical approach. Have you tried combining B-Tree and GIN composite indexes on columns used in both equality checks and full-text search?

storyContent: Protect your API from abuse with sliding window rate limiting backed by Redis sorted sets. Fixed windows are vulnerable to boundary spikes. Token bucket allows short bursts while enforcing long-term average rates. Sliding window log is the most accurate approach.
storySummary: API protection with token bucket and sliding window algorithms

storyContent: N+1 queries are the most common TypeORM performance killer. Use queryBuilder with leftJoinAndSelect instead of lazy loading relations. Set your connection pool min to 5 and max to 20 per container. For bulk inserts use multi-row INSERT instead of looping save calls.
storySummary: Avoid N+1 queries and optimize TypeORM connection pooling
